meta.label: frontier-subagent
meta.system: You are answering questions about the documents supplied below. Answer from those documents only. If the documents do not settle a question, say so explicitly rather than guessing. Be specific: give figures, names and dates exactly as they appear. Keep answers under 200 words.
harness_caveats: MODEL VERSION IS NOT PINNED. The Agent tool's model enum is sonnet/opus/haiku/fable and resolves to the running Claude Code session's model. This arm cannot answer a question about a specific release and must not be labelled as if it did.
NO TOKEN ACCOUNTING. The transport exposes no prompt_tokens or completion_tokens, so every token field is null and F90's output-volume rule cannot be applied to this arm.

WALL TIME IS NOT A LATENCY MEASUREMENT. It includes subagent scheduling, is measured under concurrency, and has no serving config behind it. It must NOT be compared against the local arms' success_at_30s or conditional TTCA - those figures are meaningless here and are recorded as null.

THE PACK IS READ FROM A FILE rather than inlined in the request, because a 140,526-character prompt is impractical to pass inline. The material is byte-identical; the delivery differs, and that is a harness difference.
NO SERVING CONFIG. There is no -c, no temperature, no reasoning setting and no build - the opposite of what Rule 8 requires of a benchmark arm.

records.question: This material contains advice that explicitly corrects an earlier recommendation. Identify which recommendation was corrected, and state what the correction was based on.
records.answer: The recommendation for conditional tool calls. Originally advised "Mistral only" based on measurement on 3 tasks; this was corrected on 2026-08-16 as E45 testing on the full set of 13 tasks showed Mistral is actually the worst arm (38%), scoring 0/5 on every category-routing, tool-selection and compound-condition task across the larger dataset.

records.question: A client needs a statutory deadline counted across a calendar. Which model does this material tell you to use, and which does it explicitly tell you NOT to use for this?
records.answer: Qwen3.8-27B. Do not use the workhorse (Qwen3-30B-A3B) for this at all. The workhorse scores 0 of 8 on counted periods - "Not one deadline, not one interest calculation, not one notice period" - whereas Qwen3.8 gets 7 of 8 on questions requiring walking a period.

records.question: For a batch of hard coding problems, this material recommends a model and a specific setting. State the wall-time ratio against the alternative it is compared with, and both absolute wall-time figures.
records.answer: Qwen3.8-27B with reasoning_effort: medium for hard coding problems, at 94x the wall time compared to Qwen3-Coder: 6,223 seconds against 66 seconds.

records.question: Does this material recommend Mistral-Small-24B for tool calls whose behaviour depends on a condition? Answer yes or no and give the supporting figure.
records.answer: No. The material states that Mistral-Small-24B scored 38% on conditional tool calls and is "the WORST arm on the full set (38%): it scores 0/5 on every category-routing, tool-selection and compound-condition task." The routing guide explicitly recommends Qwen3.8-27B at reasoning_effort: medium (86%) for tool calls whose behavior depends on a condition.

records.question: Summarise, in no more than four sentences, why this material argues that a latency figure on its own cannot be interpreted.
records.answer: A latency figure measured on one type of work does not transfer to another type of work, even on the same model and hardware. The qwen38-report demonstrated that multi-token prediction achieved a 2x speed improvement on structured legal reasoning but only 30% acceptance on ordinary conversation, showing identical implementation produces different latency depending on workload. Similarly, offering tools as available changes model behavior and latency on every request, including ones that never use them, meaning a speed measurement without documenting context produces an incomplete or misleading number. The material argues that performance is a property of model plus workload plus configuration together, which is why they stopped quoting single latency figures and started attaching the full measurement context to every number.

records.question: This material identifies gpt-oss-120b as the strongest candidate for difficult work on one axis, while placing an operational restriction on it. State the restriction and the reason given for it.
records.answer: Restriction: must not be left running unattended. Reason given: the model hung on first load and produced nothing, and the cause remains unknown.

records.question: Draft a short note (5 sentences maximum) to a colleague who wants to run a large model benchmark while a big download is in progress. Tell them whether to proceed and why, citing the specific risk.
records.answer: Do not proceed. A concurrent large download during a near-edge model benchmark creates the exact memory-pressure trigger documented in docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md (findings F24, F27, F28). When model weights plus file-cache reads from the download exceed 128 GB RAM, the amdgpu driver's SDMA suballocator deadlocks in an unkillable D-state kernel path. Recovery requires a hard physical power cycle - a graceful reboot stalls on the wedged task and leaves the box unreachable. Run the download first, let VRAM return to baseline, then start the benchmark when the machine is otherwise quiet.

records.question: For creating a Word document or driving office tools agentically, which model does this material recommend, and which model does it say refuses the task outright?
records.answer: For creating a Word document or driving office tools agentically, Qwen3-30B-A3B is recommended with 91% mean success and 0 format leaks in 110 calls (E33). Mistral refuses these tasks outright without a hand-supplied tool template.

records.question: For a long advisory session with documents arriving as you go, which model is recommended? State the specific risk this material says changes over a long session - and say explicitly whether accuracy decayed.
records.answer: Qwen3.8-27B. The specific risk that changes over a long session is resistance - the willingness to contradict you - not accuracy. As documented in the 29-turn conversation measured 2026-08-17, nothing decayed on any model: five questions asked twice came back identical, corrections made early were still applied twenty thousand tokens later, and no model quoted the wrong agreement's figure. However, the workhorse showed vulnerability at depth: when told a 60-day payment period against a document stating thirty, its wrong answer landed exactly on the user's figure, whereas Qwen3.8-27B adopted neither. Accuracy did not decay; what was lost was the model's resistance to adopting user-asserted figures.

records.question: If a model must fit in under 5 GiB, which one does this material recommend, and what are the TWO limits it names?
records.answer: Qwen3-8B with reasoning ON. Its context tops out at 40,960 tokens, and enable_thinking: false costs 4 points on the easy tier with every arithmetic item flipping to wrong.

records.question: Draft a short note (5 sentences maximum) to a colleague who is about to put a single tokens-per-second figure in a client report. Tell them what is wrong with that and what to report instead.
records.answer: A single tokens-per-second figure is misleading because speed varies dramatically with both the workload tested and the concurrency level - the same model can differ 2-3x between single-stream and multi-stream serving. Single-stream does not saturate the GPU and is the least representative point possible. Always report both aggregate throughput (what users experience, including latency) and capacity (what the hardware delivers at steady state), measured at multiple concurrency levels. Pair every speed figure with the exact workload type and conditions it was measured under, because a speed number from one kind of work does not transfer to another. Never quote a naked figure - the conditions ARE the finding.

records.question: One model is described as the strongest on a document/knowledge evaluation whose strength then failed to carry over to agentic coding work. Name that model, and say what the material tells you to use instead for interactive coding.
records.answer: Qwen3-30B-A3B (the workhorse). Use Qwen3-Coder-30B for interactive coding, with GLM-4.7-Flash as fallback.

records.question: The R&D PROGRAMME document (not the harness rules) sets out a primary and a secondary metric that must always be reported together. Name both, and say why the secondary one cannot be quoted alone.
records.answer: The two metrics are success-at-deadline (primary) and conditional TTCA (secondary). The secondary metric cannot be quoted alone because it is undefined on a wrong answer and infinite on a hang, so any central tendency computed over it has silently dropped exactly the cases the programme exists to study. A median hides the tail where non-termination lives. The document states: "A conditional TTCA quoted without its success-at-deadline figure is not a result." The conditioning (computed over successes only) must be visible with the success count beside it.
